Hi Tom / Jonas — quick note from ops: when an event is forwarded by an external system or by certain mobile clients, Google sometimes strips the TZID token and leaves just a local timestamp. In that case the calendar client treats the hour as "floating" and displays it in the recipient's local zone without conversion. That explains seeing 02:00 AM JST if the original (11:00 ET) lost its anchor.

Recommendation: please do not forward the original invite chain. Instead, Jonas, create a new event with the start time set explicitly in Asia/Tokyo (e.g., 11:00 JST) and add ACME's APAC address directly so the invite is generated with that TZID. I can also generate a regional invite per attendee (one for JST, one for ET) and mark them as the same meeting in the description to avoid duplicate joins.

Attachment: Bellwether-demo-agenda.pdf

—Soojin
Soojin Lee
